title: Transient bioelectric states can rewrite false pattern memories in animals

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Transient bioelectric states can rewrite false pattern memories in animals

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Modulating a transient bioelectric state is a conserved mechanism by which false pattern memories (altered target morphologies) can be written into the genetically specified electrical circuits of a living animal, analogous to incepting false behavioural memories in brains with optogenetics.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, much like the optogenetic techniques used to incept false behavioral memories into brains (Vetere et al., 2019), modulation of transient bioelectric state is a conserved mechanism by which false pattern memories can be re-written into the genetically-specified electrical circuits of a living animal.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Pattern Memory: A Key Component of Homeostatic Loops”. Scope: Regenerating animals, chiefly planaria

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.47

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Persistent morphology after transient voltage manipulation is measurable. Current studies test this phenomenon in restricted systems, but neither conservation nor the memory analogy is resolved by available data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether a transient measured voltage perturbation produces a persistent, heritable-through-regeneration morphology without DNA change, and whether restoring the voltage state reverses it across multiple animal systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Alternative epigenetic or tissue-state mechanisms remain.

False pattern memory is a contested interpretation.

Evidence is concentrated in planaria rather than showing a conserved animal mechanism.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.3
discriminating power: 0.42
data existence: 0.52
operationalizability: 0.54
analysis feasibility: 0.58

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A regenerative target that outlasts a transient gap-junction or channel treatment is documented for planaria in published penetrance data and, where curated, in Planform. Calling that change a false pattern memory, and a conserved mechanism across animals, goes beyond those head-number records. Tissue state and expression can carry the same persistence, and other taxa are thinly covered.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply a transient bioelectric perturbation, remove it, and test whether a new regenerative target persists across further amputations; the memory reading holds if the new target remains after tissue composition and channel expression have returned to the original state.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The optogenetic analogy is not a separate measurement.

Data are concentrated in planaria, while the claim says the mechanism is conserved across regenerating animals.

A lasting change in cell composition or channel expression is a non-memory account of the same regenerative outcome.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.5
data existence: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.45
discriminating power: 0.4
